guide.title: Emergency Drug Formulary
guide.lead: The core prehospital drugs on one page: what they're for, the usual adult dose and the one thing that stops you giving them. Your protocol sets the exact doses and who may give them; check the full formulary for children.

flashcards.question: Seven rights
flashcards.answer: Right patient, drug, dose, route, time, documentation, and the right to refuse.

flashcards.question: Nitroglycerin
flashcards.answer: 0.4 mg sublingual every 5 minutes, up to 3. Not if SBP below 90 mmHg or PDE-5 inhibitor (24 hours sildenafil/vardenafil, 48 hours tadalafil).

flashcards.question: Epinephrine doses
flashcards.answer: Anaphylaxis: 0.01 mg/kg IM (maximum 0.5 mg) of 1 mg/mL, outer thigh. Arrest: 1 mg IV/IO of 0.1 mg/mL every 3–5 minutes.

flashcards.question: Aspirin
flashcards.answer: 162–325 mg chewed for suspected ACS: faster absorption.

flashcards.question: Naloxone duration
flashcards.answer: 30–90 minutes: shorter than many opioids. Watch for re-sedation.

flashcards.question: Glucagon
flashcards.answer: 1 mg IM (0.5 mg under 25 kg). Works in about 10 minutes; needs liver glycogen; often causes vomiting.

flashcards.question: Albuterol
flashcards.answer: 2.5–5 mg nebulised, repeat every 20 minutes up to 3. Side effects: tachycardia, tremor, anxiety.

flashcards.question: Atropine in arrest?
flashcards.answer: No: removed from arrest algorithms (no benefit). Used for symptomatic bradycardia: 1 mg, up to 3 mg.

flashcards.question: Ondansetron
flashcards.answer: 4 mg IV, IM or dissolving tablet. Caution with long QT and other QT-prolonging drugs.

flashcards.question: Fentanyl vs morphine
flashcards.answer: Fentanyl: about 100 times more potent, lasts 30–60 minutes. Morphine: 3–5 hours, more histamine release and hypotension.

critical.scenario: Nursing home: 78-year-old on metoprolol and metformin, confused and sweaty, glucose 42 mg/dL. He follows commands and swallows safely.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Oral glucose 15 g, recheck in 15 minutes; glucagon IM or IV dextrose if he worsens or can't swallow; look for the cause

critical.explanation: Beta-blockers hide the warning tremor and tachycardia.
critical.kpi: Selects the correct glucose route for level of consciousness

critical.scenario: 24-year-old after a break-up: hyperventilating, crying, 'I can't breathe'; SpO₂ 100%, clear lungs, no hives or swelling. A bystander hands you an EpiPen.
critical.question: Give epinephrine?

options.t: No: no signs of anaphylaxis. Calm reassurance, coached breathing, rule out other causes

options.f: Causes tachycardia and anxiety without benefit.

critical.explanation: Right indication is part of every drug decision.
critical.kpi: Withholds a drug without an indication

critical.scenario: 66-year-old on digoxin, metoprolol and warfarin, 3 days of diarrhoea: confused, HR 52 irregular, BP 82/56.
critical.question: Likely cause and drug considerations?

options.t: Digoxin toxicity from dehydration: monitor, IV fluids, atropine if bradycardia is symptomatic, transport for levels and antidote

critical.explanation: Digoxin-specific antibody is the hospital antidote.
critical.kpi: Recognizes digoxin toxicity and avoids harmful drugs
